title: Flat terms of the explicit affine alternating Cech model
statement: For a separated f:X -> Spec A, a finite family U:Fin r -> X.Opens consisting of affine opens, and an O_X-module G flat over f [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], every integer-degree term of the explicit complex K [def-pc-affine-alternating-cech-model] is a flat O_Spec A-module [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. No cover, quasi-coherence, derived counit, or base-change conclusion is assumed.

proof.text: Separatedness of f and affineness of Spec A give separatedness of X. Mathlib IsAffineOpen.iInf makes every increasing-tuple intersection affine. Evaluate [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] on this intersection and the top affine base open. Restrict scalars along GammaSpecIso, a ring isomorphism, and use RingHom.Flat.of_bijective and Module.Flat.trans to obtain flatness for the A-action used by [def-pc-affine-alternating-cech-model]. The natural-degree term is a finite product; identify it with a dependent direct sum using DFinsupp.linearEquivFunOnFintype and use the flat direct-sum instance. This also applies to the empty family and to degrees with no tuples.

For any integer i in the image of embeddingUpNat, map extendXIso through restrictScalars and transport the natural-degree flatness along its linear equivalence. Outside that image the extended term is zero by isZero_extend_X. RestrictScalars preserves zero objects, so the underlying module is subsingleton, free and flat. Apply [lem-pc-flat-module-tilde] to each of these flat A-modules. By the definition of [def-pc-affine-alternating-cech-model] these associated sheaves are exactly the terms claimed to be flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].
